raw.description:
About the Role

Payroll isn't just numbers on a spreadsheet. It's the promise the company keeps to every employee, every pay cycle, no matter which state or territory they call home. As our Payroll Analyst, you'll be the technical and regulatory authority who makes sure that promise never breaks. You'll own end-to-end payroll settlement execution and tax compliance for a fully remote, all-states-and-territories workforce, and you'll be the connective tissue between Payroll and Accounting, making sure Finance leadership always has clear, trustworthy payroll reporting to work from.

This role is built on a clean separation of duties: you execute with precision after approval, and you guard compliance independently. That combination of executor and compliance guardian is what keeps our financial integrity and audit readiness rock solid.

What You'll Do

Settlement Execution 

  • Execute payroll settlement following the Senior Manager, Accounting's approval: bank upload, 401(k)/HSA remittances, post-payroll sign-off 
  • Process cancel/correct actions only under documented authorization from the Senior Manager, Accounting 
  • Prepare settlement summary reports for Finance leadership 

Tax Compliance 

  • Upload tax notifications to the HRIS as received to maintain compliance across state and local tax jurisdictions 
  • Analyze payroll tax variances and reconciliation items; escalate anomalies to the Senior Manager, Accounting 

Cross-Functional 

  • Serve as Finance's subject-matter expert on payroll tax and settlement questions from CX Partners and external auditors 
  • Maintain documentation supporting quarterly/annual compliance and settlement audits 
  • Provide technical guidance on payroll tax implications of new-state hiring, benefits changes, or comp structure updates 

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field; payroll certification (CPP or similar) strongly preferred 
  • 3–5+ years of experience in payroll settlement, payroll tax compliance, or multi-state payroll administration 
  • Deep knowledge of federal, state, and local payroll tax law for a remote, all-states/territories workforce 
  • Experience configuring tax and settlement modules within an HRIS platform (Paycom, Workday, ADP, UKG, or similar) 
  • Strong analytical and research skills to track and interpret evolving tax regulations 
  • Able to translate payroll and compliance details into clear, accessible updates for non-payroll audiences, including Finance leadership
  • High level of integrity and independence — this role executes settlement but does not approve its own work 

Why Join Us

At Nightingale, precision work like this ripples outward. Getting payroll right, on time, every time, is how we take care of the employees who take care of our students. If you love owning the details, protecting the integrity of a process, and being the person people trust to get compliance right, we'd love to talk.

Budgeted Hiring Range
$68,010.20—$80,012 USD

All new hires are required to attend New Collaborator Orientation (NCO) in Salt Lake City, Utah. The College will cover travel, lodging, and other accommodations.

Nightingale’s commitment to diversity and inclusion is reflected both in our learners and collaborators because we believe the best outcomes for learners from underserved and diverse populations are achieved through collaborators with similar backgrounds and cultures. Nightingale Education Group is an equal opportunity employer.

Our Mission (not just words on the wall, we live it, love it, and daily contribute to it): With the primary focus on higher learning in healthcare professions, Nightingale Education Group contributes to elevating education, health, and employment systems through facilitation of academic achievement, personal growth, and professional development of its learners, alumni, and collaborators, while serving diverse communities.

At Nightingale Education Group, our Innovative Education model helps transform rural health landscapes through our blended-distance learning platform. Every person involved with Nightingale Education Group helps to change the lives of our learners, our communities, and ultimately the world by adding to the quality of healthcare. We are proud to have graduated nearly 5,000 nurses serving communities in need. We are serious about our outcomes and have a little bit of fun getting there.

The professional and personal development of our learners and our collaborators is our company’s foundation. Not only do we develop strategies that promote a positive work-life integration, but we also create an environment that invites you to become an expert in your field, be it through higher education or professional development. Put simply, we elevate employment, elevate health, and elevate education. We’re so happy that you’ve found us!

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check and drug screen.

Alpha Online entwickelt die Prozessmanagement-Software für den professionellen Gebrauchtwagenhandel in Deutschland. Unser Kernprodukt AlphaController steuert alle Arbeitsprozesse im Autohaus – von der Fahrzeugbewertung bis zum Verkauf. Zu unseren Kunden zählen Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Volkswagen, Porsche und Audi. One Platform. One Profit Engine.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du betreust einen festen Kundenstamm aus Autohäusern und Autohausgruppen und bist ihre erste Ansprechperson für alles rund um den AlphaController
  • Du berätst Kunden bei der Gestaltung ihrer internen Prozesse, vom Fahrzeugankauf bis zum Verkauf
  • Du hältst Präsentationen und leitest Workshops für die Teams, die täglich mit der Software arbeiten
  • Du erkennst, wo Kunden das Produkt noch nicht ausschöpfen, und machst konkrete Vorschläge
  • Du steuerst Anforderungen und Fehlermeldungen aus dem Kundenkontakt als Tickets in Jira an die Entwicklung
  • Du dokumentierst deine Kundenfälle sauber in unseren Systemen

Du startest mit einer intensiven Einarbeitungsphase direkt bei der Geschäftsführung und lernst Produkt, Kunden und Markt von innen kennen. Danach entscheiden wir gemeinsam, ob dein Schwerpunkt im Customer Success oder im Kunden-Onboarding liegt.

Was du mitbringst

  • Deutsch auf C2-Niveau in Wort und Schrift
  • Interesse an komplexen Softwareprodukten und die Bereitschaft, dich tief einzuarbeiten
  • Lust auf direkten Kundenkontakt, am Telefon, im Video-Call und vor Ort im Autohaus
  • Strukturierte, analytische Arbeitsweise: du behältst mehrere Kunden parallel im Blick
  • IT-Affinität im Alltag: Webanwendungen, Microsoft 365 und Slack sind für dich Routine

Von Vorteil

  • Erste Berührungspunkte mit Kundenkontakt, ob aus Praktikum, Werkstudentenjob oder Ausbildung
  • Erfahrung aus dem Automobilhandel oder dem Autohaus-Alltag
  • KI-affine Arbeitsweise: du nutzt Tools wie Claude, ChatGPT oder Copilot aktiv im Arbeitsalltag
  • Erfahrung mit Jira, Salesforce oder vergleichbaren Tools

Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Unbefristete Festanstellung mit attraktiver Vergütung
  • Nahezu 100 % Remote – Wohnsitz in Deutschland erforderlich
  • Flexibles Homeoffice
  • Ein Umfeld, in dem KI und Digitalisierung echte Rolle spielen – kein Lippenbekenntnis
  • Erfahrenes Team mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen
  • Mitarbeiter-Benefits

Bewirb dich jetzt – dein Lebenslauf reicht.

raw.description:
We are seeking an innovative and strategic Digital Product Manager to lead the vision, roadmap, and delivery of a key digital product within our organization. This role will serve as the bridge between business partners, technology teams, and end users to ensure product strategy is clearly aligned to business objectives, customer needs, and long-term enterprise priorities.

The Digital Product Manager will operate within an agile, sprint-based delivery model and will be responsible for translating business goals into actionable product requirements, prioritized backlogs, and measurable outcomes. This individual will work closely with cross-functional stakeholders to define product opportunities, evaluate customer and operational pain points, and guide the development of digital solutions that improve efficiency, engagement, and overall user experience.

A successful candidate will bring a forward-looking product mindset, strong business acumen, and a deep understanding of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. This role requires someone who can identify where AI, automation, data, and modern digital capabilities can create meaningful business value while ensuring solutions remain practical, scalable, and aligned to stakeholder needs.

Job Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Own the product vision, strategy, roadmap, and backlog for a specific digital product.
  • Partner with business leaders to ensure product priorities align with strategic objectives and measurable business outcomes.
  • Work closely with IT, design, data, operations, and other cross-functional teams to deliver product enhancements through an agile sprint model.
  • Translate business needs into clear epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and sprint-ready requirements.
  • Prioritize product work based on customer value, business impact, technical feasibility, compliance needs, and delivery capacity.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage AI, automation, analytics, and digital tools to improve customer experience, operational efficiency, and product performance.
  • Lead stakeholder discussions, sprint planning, backlog refinement, demos, and product performance reviews.
  • Monitor product metrics, user feedback, and market trends to continuously improve the product.
  • Serve as the primary product voice between business partners and technology delivery teams.

Key Result Areas

  • Establish and track objectives & key results (KPIs), such as engagement, conversion, customer satisfaction, and/or internal efficiency, to support our Service Excellence philosophy and drive measurable business impact
  • Deliver user-centric digital products that enhance customer experience and internal operations, validated through evidence-based learning and iterative launches

Qualifications:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must have the following education and/or experience:

  • 5+ years of experience in digital product management or a related field, with a proven track record of delivering successful digital products
  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, Business, Engineering, or a related discipline)
  • Demonstrated expertise in digital product management, including supporting complex software development projects, defining product requirements, and delivering scalable platforms that meet user and business needs.
  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (software developers, designers, data analysts, compliance specialists) and stakeholders
  • Excellent communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to contribute to consensus in a collaborative environment.
  • Proficiency in a product development lifecycle and with agile methodologies
  • Experience with user research (e.g., user interviews, usability testing) and product discovery (e.g., rapid experimentation, hypothesis testing)
  • Experience with the mortgage industry (origination and/or servicing) preferred
  • Experience leveraging AI in product development or daily workflows (e.g., predictive analytics, NLP, chatbots, intelligent document processing) is a plus
  • Experience in at least one of the following areas is a plus: consumer-facing digital products (e.g., online platforms, mobile apps), team member experience tools or internal tools, document/data automation (e.g., intelligent document processing), or omni-channel communications tools

Training / Licensing Requirements:

  • Must pass the Company’s Background Screening process prior to beginning employment. Additionally, as a condition of employment, you may be required to pass client-specific background check requirements or Federal/State licensing requirements, if applicable.

The salary range for this position is expected to be $120,000 – $130,000 per year, depending on geographic location, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate. This position is also eligible for annual bonus based on performance and subject to the terms of the Company’s applicable plans.

raw.description:
Role Title: Military Writing Specialist

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote (US Only)

micro1 is engaging Military Writing Specialists to support a unique project, leveraging expertise in military writing and reporting. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. Contributors will use their background in Department of War (Department of Defense) documentation to generate, review, and evaluate a wide range of reports, summaries, and status updates reflective of authentic military processes. Your input will help develop benchmarks and grading guidelines that will teach AI to understand and replicate effective, compliant government communication.

Scope of Work

  1. Create realistic military and federal status reports, summaries, and executive updates based on prompts and supplied artifacts.
  2. Develop “golden responses” that demonstrate high-quality, standards-aligned reporting for use in AI model training.
  3. Draft grading rubrics and guidelines that reflect best practices in federal and military writing assessment.
  4. Evaluate AI-generated reports, providing detailed feedback in both written and verbal form.
  5. Share context on stylistic differences and individual approaches to common military documents (e.g., WARs, SITREPs, AARs, executive summaries).
  6. Produce supporting documents such as decision briefs, memoranda, and action officer updates when required.
  7. Collaborate with other subject matter experts to ensure diversity of reporting styles and adherence to branch-specific terminology.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Former U.S. Department of War (Department of Defense) professional with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
  2. Experience producing templated and standard reports such as Weekly Activity Reports (WARs), Situation Reports (SITREPs), After-Action Reviews, or similar artifacts.
  3. Expertise spanning two or more branches of the U.S. military is a plus; a diverse background across roles is highly valued.
  4. Proven proficiency in written and verbal communication, particularly in conveying technical or operational subject matter.
  5. Demonstrated ability to craft, grade, and review back office documents, PowerPoints, memos, and spreadsheets for military or federal purposes.
  6. US-based contributor with broad familiarity with federal documentation standards and compliance best practices.
  7. Comfortable collaborating remotely and sharing insights on nuanced, highly procedural reporting tasks.

raw.description:
• Location: Remote — U.S.-based required. For this opening we give preference to candidates based in the Central or Mountain time zones; all zones are considered if the coverage window below genuinely works for your life.

  • Reports to: Head of Sales

About Breathe for Change

Breathe for Change (B4C) is building the category of Human Intelligence in Education to address the crises of educator stress and burnout, student mental health, and AI disruption. Our accredited higher-education programs — anchored by our Master's of Education — equip educators with the human skills they and their students need most to thrive. We envision a world where school is about what truly matters: empowering students AND teachers to live purposeful, creative lives full of vitality, wholeness, and connection.

The role

You'll be a full-cycle inside sales professional guiding teachers through the decision to enroll in B4C's degree programs. Marketing fills your calendar with booked 1:1 phone calls — you run a consultative discovery conversation, help each educator reach an honest fit decision, and enroll the ones the program genuinely serves.

Know what you'd be selling: a Master's degree our graduates consistently describe as transformative — for their teaching, their wellbeing, and their lives. Every enrollment you close is a teacher who stays in the profession stronger than they came to it. Most sales jobs ask you to believe in the product as a professional courtesy; this one earns it.

Three things to know about how we work, because they tell you whether this seat is for you:

You'd be joining an awesome team

This is a small group of mission-driven professionals who genuinely like each other and are unusually good at what they do. We chase a team goal — the number belongs to all of us, not to a leaderboard of individuals — so the incentive is to make the person next to you better. Reps trade what's working in real time, review each other's calls in the film room, and celebrate each other's wins loudly. If you've worked somewhere the top closer hoarded their tricks and the floor went quiet when someone was behind, this will feel different on day one.

We take selling seriously as a craft

Our motion is documented and built from what our best people actually do, not from theory — most of our wins close on the first substantive conversation, carried by disciplined follow-up. Everything we've built around it — the playbook, the coaching, the AI tooling — exists to get you to full speed fast: weeks, not quarters. After that, the book is yours to run. There are no individual volume quotas and no commission — we make sure you have a strong, steady set of calls, flexing up and down a bit during the highest-demand weeks and months, but overall protecting your calendar against getting overloaded. We hire people who run their own week, and then we get out of the way.

We sell with integrity, structurally

Teachers are trust professionals and our buyers for life — pressure tactics, false urgency, and manufactured scarcity don't just violate our values, they're incompatible with how we're regulated and how we retain students. Honest disqualification is a celebrated outcome. The product is what makes this possible: our graduates rate the program at an NPS in the +70s, so the honest conversation and the effective one are the same conversation. If your best work happens when you're allowed to tell a prospect the truth, you'll like it here.

What you'll actually do

  • Run ~8–12 scheduled discovery calls a day* (20 minutes each) with teachers who booked time to talk about the M.Ed. — assess fit, run real discovery, answer program and financing questions, and ask for the enrollment decision when the signal is there. *Daily volume fluctuates with seasonality, events, and experience.

  • Own the follow-up between calls: short, purposeful texting that protects shows and carries momentum, completion calls that finish decisions, and the follow-through that means nothing you promised a teacher ever slips.

  • Sell when teachers can talk. During the school year our calls concentrate in two windows: teachers' planning/lunch periods (roughly noon–2pm ET) and after school (roughly 4–8pm ET); in summer the weight shifts earlier. Your core coverage window is approximately noon–8pm ET on weekdays — in Central or Mountain time that's an ordinary late-morning-to-early-evening day, which is why we prefer those zones. Our best reps design their week around the teacher's clock on purpose; this role requires that design to be genuine and sustainable, not overtime.

  • Hand each newly enrolled educator cleanly to our onboarding team. Your job is the decision — a dedicated team carries students from deposit to day one, so your selling time stays selling time.

  • Bring what you learn back to the team: film-room participation, script feedback, sharing what's working. Our playbook carries our reps' wording because their wording works.

Who we're looking for

  • A proven consultative closer. 2+ years in a full-cycle closing role — high-consideration B2C (education, financial services, insurance, home services, coaching/wellness programs) or similar consultative sales — with a track record you can quantify and explain how it was measured.

  • One-conversation instincts. You know how to earn a decision in the first call when the fit is real — discovery first, then a direct, unapologetic ask — and how to walk away warmly when it isn't.

  • Follow-through as craft. You can describe the actual system you use to keep 100+ open conversations from slipping. Organized is table stakes; we're looking for someone who treats follow-up as the job, not the interruption.

  • A fast, eager tool adopter. This role runs on systems — a CRM (HubSpot a plus), AI-assisted call review and coaching, texting and scheduling tools, Google Workspace — and the stack keeps getting better. You don't just tolerate new tools; you pick them up quickly, fold them into how you work, and treat them as part of the craft.

  • A calendar owner. You manage your own energy and hours like a professional athlete — boundaries, blocks, evening selling by design, recovery budgeted after surges.

  • A teammate on purpose. Our reps get better in public — film-room reviews, script feedback, lending your wording to the playbook when it works. You want colleagues who sharpen your game and you return the favor; closers who guard their tricks don't thrive here.

  • Mission-resonant. You care that the thing you're selling genuinely changes teachers' lives, and you can say why in your own words. Our best closers are here on purpose — selling work that matters is the point.

You do NOT need admissions, higher-ed, or education-industry experience. We'll teach you the domain, the program, and the playbook — that's what our onboarding and coaching system is for. What we can't teach in eight weeks is professional selling. If you're a great closer who has always wanted your work to mean something, this is the seat.

Growth

This role has a real career ladder: EDC → Senior EDC, with promotion earned on craft, ownership, team impact, and judgment — assessed from your actual work, not tenure. Our most recent Senior promotion went to a rep whose calls became the film-room examples the team learns from. We promote from within on purpose.

Why this seat

Sales careers rarely offer all three: a product with real outcomes, a team of mission-driven professionals who treat selling as a craft worth studying and pull for each other, and a mission you'd defend at dinner. Teachers are holding up the hardest job in America, and the ones who find us are looking for a way to grow without leaving the classroom. You'd be the person who helps them decide well. If you've been waiting for a reason to bring your best selling somewhere it counts, this is it.

Compensation & benefits

  • Base salary: $80,000–$100,000, depending on experience and demonstrated track record

  • Equity eligibility (varies by experience)

  • Health, vision, and dental insurance

  • 401k and FSA/HSA eligibility

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Note: per our accreditation and Title IV compliance posture, compensation is never linked to enrollment counts — raises and promotions are earned on craft and professional factors. (Stated here because good salespeople always ask.)

How to apply

The application asks five short questions — they matter more than your résumé, and we read every answer.

Breathe for Change is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Compensation Range: $80K - $100K

This is a hands-on, execution-focused role. You will work closely with recruiters and hiring managers to keep hiring moving smoothly and accurately. It’s a good fit for someone early in their career who wants to learn how high-quality technical hiring actually works in practice.

  • Support recruiting projects and process improvements as the team scales, including candidate experience and employer branding initiatives.

  • Help keep hiring operations organised, responsive, and moving at pace.

What you will need

  • 0–2 years of experience in recruiting, HR, operations, coordination, or related roles
    (fresh graduates with a strong interest in recruiting are welcome).

  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.

  • Comfort working with tools such as Google Sheets / Excel and basic ATS systems.

Role Title: Data Entry Keyer

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging Data Entry Keyers to contribute to a customer's advanced AI benchmark project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Design and produce expert-level evaluation tasks that simulate real-world data entry and validation challenges for AI agents.
  2. Construct and curate large, complex datasets—including CSVs, PDFs, spreadsheets, and technical documents filled with realistic errors such as malformed records, missing data, and inconsistent formats.
  3. Define the correct final state for each task, specifying the exact error cases and reconciliation requirements that an AI must address.
  4. Author detailed grading rubrics (35+ criteria) for assessment of AI agent outputs, focusing on both accuracy and completeness in error detection.
  5. Ensure all authored tasks mirror the authentic complexity and standards of highly regulated or audit-sensitive environments.
  6. Collaborate asynchronously through precise written and verbal communication to iterate and refine evaluation materials.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Extensive experience in data entry, quality assurance, or data validation within regulated or audit-sensitive domains such as healthcare claims, finance back office, or legal operations.
  2. Demonstrated ability to achieve and document high accuracy standards, including measurable error rates and outcomes.
  3. Strong skills in detecting and analyzing data inconsistencies, silent truncations, and formatting irregularities across diverse file types.
  4. Proficient written English, enabling clear drafting of complex evaluation tasks and comprehensive grading rubrics.
  5. Exceptional attention to detail and a disciplined, process-oriented work style.
  6. Experience contributing to projects with high stakes for compliance, accuracy, or data integrity is highly valued.
  7. Comfort working independently and communicating proactively within remote, distributed project environments.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.

Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

About Breathe for Change

Breathe for Change (B4C) is building the category of Human Intelligence in Education to address the crises of educator stress and burnout, student mental health, and AI disruption. Our accredited higher-education programs — anchored by our Master's of Education — equip educators with the human skills they and their students need most to thrive. We envision a world where school is about what truly matters: empowering students AND teachers to live purposeful, creative lives full of vitality, wholeness, and connection.

The role

You'll be a full-cycle inside sales professional guiding teachers through the decision to enroll in B4C's degree programs. Marketing fills your calendar with booked 1:1 phone calls — you run a consultative discovery conversation, help each educator reach an honest fit decision, and enroll the ones the program genuinely serves.

Know what you'd be selling: a Master's degree our graduates consistently describe as transformative — for their teaching, their wellbeing, and their lives. Every enrollment you close is a teacher who stays in the profession stronger than they came to it. Most sales jobs ask you to believe in the product as a professional courtesy; this one earns it.

Three things to know about how we work, because they tell you whether this seat is for you:

You'd be joining an awesome team

This is a small group of mission-driven professionals who genuinely like each other and are unusually good at what they do. We chase a team goal — the number belongs to all of us, not to a leaderboard of individuals — so the incentive is to make the person next to you better. Reps trade what's working in real time, review each other's calls in the film room, and celebrate each other's wins loudly. If you've worked somewhere the top closer hoarded their tricks and the floor went quiet when someone was behind, this will feel different on day one.

We take selling seriously as a craft

Our motion is documented and built from what our best people actually do, not from theory — most of our wins close on the first substantive conversation, carried by disciplined follow-up. Everything we've built around it — the playbook, the coaching, the AI tooling — exists to get you to full speed fast: weeks, not quarters. After that, the book is yours to run. There are no individual volume quotas and no commission — we make sure you have a strong, steady set of calls, flexing up and down a bit during the highest-demand weeks and months, but overall protecting your calendar against getting overloaded. We hire people who run their own week, and then we get out of the way.

We sell with integrity, structurally

Teachers are trust professionals and our buyers for life — pressure tactics, false urgency, and manufactured scarcity don't just violate our values, they're incompatible with how we're regulated and how we retain students. Honest disqualification is a celebrated outcome. The product is what makes this possible: our graduates rate the program at an NPS in the +70s, so the honest conversation and the effective one are the same conversation. If your best work happens when you're allowed to tell a prospect the truth, you'll like it here.

What you'll actually do

  • Run ~8–12 scheduled discovery calls a day* (20 minutes each) with teachers who booked time to talk about the M.Ed. — assess fit, run real discovery, answer program and financing questions, and ask for the enrollment decision when the signal is there. *Daily volume fluctuates with seasonality, events, and experience.

  • Own the follow-up between calls: short, purposeful texting that protects shows and carries momentum, completion calls that finish decisions, and the follow-through that means nothing you promised a teacher ever slips.

  • Sell when teachers can talk. During the school year our calls concentrate in two windows: teachers' planning/lunch periods (roughly noon–2pm ET) and after school (roughly 4–8pm ET); in summer the weight shifts earlier. Your core coverage window is approximately noon–8pm ET on weekdays — in Central or Mountain time that's an ordinary late-morning-to-early-evening day, which is why we prefer those zones. Our best reps design their week around the teacher's clock on purpose; this role requires that design to be genuine and sustainable, not overtime.

  • Hand each newly enrolled educator cleanly to our onboarding team. Your job is the decision — a dedicated team carries students from deposit to day one, so your selling time stays selling time.

  • Bring what you learn back to the team: film-room participation, script feedback, sharing what's working. Our playbook carries our reps' wording because their wording works.

Who we're looking for

  • A proven consultative closer. 2+ years in a full-cycle closing role — high-consideration B2C (education, financial services, insurance, home services, coaching/wellness programs) or similar consultative sales — with a track record you can quantify and explain how it was measured.

  • One-conversation instincts. You know how to earn a decision in the first call when the fit is real — discovery first, then a direct, unapologetic ask — and how to walk away warmly when it isn't.

  • Follow-through as craft. You can describe the actual system you use to keep 100+ open conversations from slipping. Organized is table stakes; we're looking for someone who treats follow-up as the job, not the interruption.

  • A fast, eager tool adopter. This role runs on systems — a CRM (HubSpot a plus), AI-assisted call review and coaching, texting and scheduling tools, Google Workspace — and the stack keeps getting better. You don't just tolerate new tools; you pick them up quickly, fold them into how you work, and treat them as part of the craft.

  • A calendar owner. You manage your own energy and hours like a professional athlete — boundaries, blocks, evening selling by design, recovery budgeted after surges.

  • A teammate on purpose. Our reps get better in public — film-room reviews, script feedback, lending your wording to the playbook when it works. You want colleagues who sharpen your game and you return the favor; closers who guard their tricks don't thrive here.

  • Mission-resonant. You care that the thing you're selling genuinely changes teachers' lives, and you can say why in your own words. Our best closers are here on purpose — selling work that matters is the point.

You do NOT need admissions, higher-ed, or education-industry experience. We'll teach you the domain, the program, and the playbook — that's what our onboarding and coaching system is for. What we can't teach in eight weeks is professional selling. If you're a great closer who has always wanted your work to mean something, this is the seat.

Growth

This role has a real career ladder: EDC → Senior EDC, with promotion earned on craft, ownership, team impact, and judgment — assessed from your actual work, not tenure. Our most recent Senior promotion went to a rep whose calls became the film-room examples the team learns from. We promote from within on purpose.

Why this seat

Sales careers rarely offer all three: a product with real outcomes, a team of mission-driven professionals who treat selling as a craft worth studying and pull for each other, and a mission you'd defend at dinner. Teachers are holding up the hardest job in America, and the ones who find us are looking for a way to grow without leaving the classroom. You'd be the person who helps them decide well. If you've been waiting for a reason to bring your best selling somewhere it counts, this is it.

Compensation & benefits

  • Base salary: $80,000–$100,000, depending on experience and demonstrated track record

  • Equity eligibility (varies by experience)

  • Health, vision, and dental insurance

  • 401k and FSA/HSA eligibility

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Note: per our accreditation and Title IV compliance posture, compensation is never linked to enrollment counts — raises and promotions are earned on craft and professional factors. (Stated here because good salespeople always ask.)

How to apply

The application asks five short questions — they matter more than your résumé, and we read every answer.

Breathe for Change is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Compensation Range: $80K - $100K

Role

This is a hands-on, execution-focused role. You will work closely with recruiters and hiring managers to keep hiring moving smoothly and accurately. It’s a good fit for someone early in their career who wants to learn how high-quality technical hiring actually works in practice.

  • Support the full recruitment process across roles, from sourcing and screening to interview coordination and offer support.

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date candidate records in the ATS, ensuring data quality and process consistency.

  • Support recruiting projects and process improvements as the team scales, including candidate experience and employer branding initiatives.

  • Help keep hiring operations organised, responsive, and moving at pace.

What you will need

  • 0–2 years of experience in recruiting, HR, operations, coordination, or related roles
    (fresh graduates with a strong interest in recruiting are welcome).

  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.

  • Comfort working with tools such as Google Sheets / Excel and basic ATS systems.

  • A proactive, learning-oriented mindset and openness to feedback.

  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and follow through reliably.

(Prior recruiting experience is helpful but not required. Attitude, curiosity, and execution matter more.)

Why join A1

  • Learn technical recruiting from the ground up in a small, high-bar team.

  • Work closely with experienced recruiters, engineers, and hiring managers.

  • Hands-on ownership and real responsibility from day one.

  • Flat structure where initiative and execution matter more than titles.

Role Title: Data Entry Keyer

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging Data Entry Keyers to contribute to a customer's advanced AI benchmark project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Design and produce expert-level evaluation tasks that simulate real-world data entry and validation challenges for AI agents.
  2. Construct and curate large, complex datasets—including CSVs, PDFs, spreadsheets, and technical documents filled with realistic errors such as malformed records, missing data, and inconsistent formats.
  3. Define the correct final state for each task, specifying the exact error cases and reconciliation requirements that an AI must address.
  4. Author detailed grading rubrics (35+ criteria) for assessment of AI agent outputs, focusing on both accuracy and completeness in error detection.
  5. Ensure all authored tasks mirror the authentic complexity and standards of highly regulated or audit-sensitive environments.
  6. Collaborate asynchronously through precise written and verbal communication to iterate and refine evaluation materials.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Extensive experience in data entry, quality assurance, or data validation within regulated or audit-sensitive domains such as healthcare claims, finance back office, or legal operations.
  2. Demonstrated ability to achieve and document high accuracy standards, including measurable error rates and outcomes.
  3. Strong skills in detecting and analyzing data inconsistencies, silent truncations, and formatting irregularities across diverse file types.
  4. Proficient written English, enabling clear drafting of complex evaluation tasks and comprehensive grading rubrics.
  5. Exceptional attention to detail and a disciplined, process-oriented work style.
  6. Experience contributing to projects with high stakes for compliance, accuracy, or data integrity is highly valued.
  7. Comfort working independently and communicating proactively within remote, distributed project environments.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.

Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

raw.description:
Finance Transformation Manager — M-KOPA

You know the difference between a demo and a system that survives contact with a trial balance. That's rarer than you think.

Most people who can talk fluently about AI have never had to make it work inside a real close process, a real audit trail, a real Anaplan model that finance actually trusts. M-KOPA is looking for someone who has — or someone ready to prove they can.

Where this sits. M-KOPA is one of Africa's fastest-growing fintechs, now serving 7 million customers across five markets and having unlocked over $2 billion in credit. Behind those numbers is a finance function running on Microsoft Dynamics and Anaplan, increasingly threaded through with Claude, and a leadership team that's decided this is the moment to stop treating AI as an experiment and start treating it as infrastructure.

Why now. We've grown from 5 million customers to 7 million, and we're building toward 10 million next. That growth doesn't just need more finance headcount — it needs a finance function that runs leaner and smarter than the one that got us here. 86% of our customers report improved quality of life, and 70% use our products to generate income; the systems behind those numbers need to scale without the manual reconciliation and reporting drag that usually comes with scale. This role exists because our leadership has committed to closing that gap now, not after it becomes a bottleneck.

What makes this different. Most "finance transformation" roles are really change-management roles wearing a technical label — you'll sit in workshops, write recommendations, and hand them to someone else to build. This one isn't that. You'll sit inside the finance team, find the friction yourself, and build the fix yourself: deepening our Claude–Dynamics integration, designing agents and workflows that actually replace manual reconciliation work, and owning the result end to end. It's a builder's mandate with a finance brief, not an IT ticket queue.

What you'll bring.

  • Demonstrable experience deploying Claude (or a comparable AI system) in a real business context — prompt design, workflow automation, API integration, and artefacts that actually run in production. This is the single most important thing we're looking for, and we'll ask you to show us something real you've built, ideally involving a Dynamics-style integration.

  • A technical foundation strong enough to read a data model and a trial balance in the same afternoon, paired with exceptional learning aptitude — the proven ability to apply AI and engineering thinking to genuinely complex financial and accounting scenarios.

  • Working knowledge of how audit actually works in practice: mining and structuring data for external and internal audit processes, and following through on remediation of findings, not just producing the report.

What the work looks like. Some weeks you're deep in the weeds of a Dynamics-Anaplan integration, chasing down why two systems disagree on a number. Other weeks you're building an agent that turns a two-day reconciliation into a two-hour one, then coaching the finance team on when to trust it and when not to. You'll be the person finance calls when something's slow, and the person engineering calls when they need someone who actually understands what a close process demands. Data integrity — one source of truth across the finance stack — sits with you.

Reality check. This role asks you to be genuinely bilingual between finance and engineering, and there's no playbook to hand you — you'll be writing it as you go, often while systems are live and numbers are due. If that sounds like friction rather than freedom, this probably isn't the role. If it sounds like exactly the kind of problem you've been waiting for someone to hand you, you're probably ready for it.

Where you work from. This role is remote or based in any of our operating markets — we're more interested in what you can build than where you build it from.

If you've spent the last while wondering why finance teams still work the way they did a decade ago, and you've actually built something that proves it doesn't have to — let's talk about what that could look like at M-KOPA scale.

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at .

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

Important Notice

M-KOPA is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to assembling a diverse, broadly trained staff. Women, minorities, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

M-KOPA explicitly prohibits the use of Forced or Child Labour and respects the rights of its employees to agree to terms and conditions of employment voluntarily, without coercion, and freely terminate their employment on appropriate notice. M-KOPA shall ensure that its Employees are of legal working age and shall comply with local laws for youth employment or student work, such as internships or apprenticeships.

M-KOPA does not collect/charge any money as a pre-employment or post-employment requirement. This means that we never ask for ‘recruitment fees’, ‘processing fees’, ‘interview fees’, or any other kind of money in exchange for offer letters or interviews at any time during the hiring process.

Applications for this position will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisting and interviews will take place at any stage during the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a suitable candidate is selected before the advertised closing date.

If your application is successful M-KOPA undertakes pre-employment background checks as part of its recruitment process, these include; criminal records, identification verification, academic qualifications, employment dates and employer references.

Come join the organization that is redefining security for the AI era. As one of the fastest-growing startups ever, we enable teams to secure cloud and AI applications by connecting code, cloud, and runtime into a single shared context. Our Wizards from all over the globe work together to protect the infrastructure of our customers, including over 65% of the Fortune 100, who trust us to scan and secure over 230 billion files daily. We’re honored to be a leading player in a massive and growing market, and we continue to look for exceptional Wizards who are eager to make a significant impact on our team. At Wiz, you’ll have the freedom to think creatively, dream big, and use your full range of skills to contribute to our momentous growth. Come join our team and help us create secure cloud environments that allow even the best companies to move faster, all while having some fun!

Summary

As a Senior Technical Account Manager (TAM), you’ll be responsible for planning and executing strategies that drive customer adoption and use of the Wiz platform for our largest customers.

Your cloud and security industry expertise will allow you to provide impactful guidance to customers throughout their Wiz onboarding and operationalization journey. You will serve as the bridge between customers and the broader Wiz team – you'll streamline collaboration between Product Management, Sales, Engineering, and Support to deliver a cohesive customer experience for our most demanding customers.

Strong technical expertise and customer-facing skills will be essential in addressing the needs of our customers. Your understanding of how large organizations leverage cloud, security, and SaaS technologies will allow you to empathize with customer personas and drive effective conversations with customer personas at all levels.

What you’ll do:

  • Be a Wiz Product and Cloud Security Expert – Serve as a trusted technical advisor throughout your customers’ Wiz journey
    • Confidently navigate customers through the deployment, configuration, and operationalization of Wiz using best practices and your existing cloud-security domain expertise.
    • Serve as the primary technical contact for your book of customers, helping to solve technical questions and issues as they arise via email, Slack, and support tickets.
    • Act proactively, by leading the customer on a journey to full adoption and value and promoting excellence in addressing Cloud, Code and Runtime security risk
    • Continuously monitor news related to emerging cloud security threats and further develop your domain expertise

  • Drive Adoption, Business Value Realization, and Customer Satisfaction – Ensure your book of customers are delighted and seeing value from their Wiz purchase
    • Help customers develop success plans with measurable goals throughout the Wiz lifecycle that align with their organizational security and compliance objectives
    • Act proactively, by leading the customer on a journey to full adoption and value, and promoting excellence in addressing Cloud, Code, and Runtime security risk

    • Actively drive value based conversations with customer executives and provide meaningful contributions to QBRs/executive briefings
  • Advocate for your Customers – Understand, document, and represent your customers’ needs to internal Wiz stakeholders
    • Capture feature requests/adoption blockers and liaise with Product and Engineering teams to determine priority and alternative solutions

Manage your book of business and support revenue objectives - Support and manage a book of up to 10 strategic customers, depending on size and complexityIdentify opportunities for expansion and assist in securing renewals in partnership with sales and renewals teams.

    • Drive towards utilization/adoption targets for your book of business
    • Identify, document, and action on risks (e.g, satisfaction/churn/renewal/health) in customer engagements

Help build and scale a world-class TAM organization at a hyper-growth company – assist in driving improvements in Wiz’s TAM motion and have an impact across GTM teams Develop documentation, mentor TAMs, and develop an area of technical subject-matter expertise

    • Partner cross-functionally with internal teams to improve processes

What you’ll bring

    • 8-12yrs of experience in technical customer-facing roles, ideally supporting a cloud / cloud-security product
      • Examples include: Senior Technical Account Manager, Senior Professional Services Engineer, Principal Solutions Engineer, Senior Technical Support Specialist, Lead Customer Success Engineer, or Sr. Architect.
    • B.S. in Computer Science, Engineering, or similar field, or equivalent advanced experience.
    • Demonstrated ability to manage nebulous job responsibilities while actively improving and developing net-new processes
  • Technical Knowledge
    • Expert understanding of cloud services and architecture of at least 2 CSPs (AWS/GCP/Azure/OCI) – ideally, you have multiple advanced CSP certifications (e.g., Certified Solutions Architect - Professional, Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional).
    • Deep familiarity with cloud-security best practices, advanced threat models, and complex CNAPP use cases. Ideally, you have a security certification (e.g., CISSP, CCSP) and extensive experience helping organizations address complex cloud-security challenges.
    • Practical experience deploying and operationalizing containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes), as well as addressing corresponding security considerations
    • Practical experience deploying and operationalizing DevOps technologies – CI/CD, Version Control Systems, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), etc., and their security implications.
    • Expert-level familiarity with Linux and Windows operating system security concepts, and advanced troubleshooting experience
    • Exceptional problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose and resolve highly complex technical issues, driving resolution across intricate and often ambiguous internal and external structures.
    • Demonstrated ability and commitment to continuously learn and master novel and emerging cloud/security technologies.
  • Account Management and Customer Success
    • Proven track record of successfully managing a book of business with 5+ complex enterprise/strategic customers.
    • Proven track record of building and maintaining executive-level relationships with enterprise/strategic clients, driving significant customer outcomes, and consistently exceeding performance targets.
    • Expert ability to continuously enable customers on the Wiz platform and proactively assist them in solving problems, ranging from trivial to highly complex and strategic.
    • Willingness to work across multiple communication channels and platforms to assist your customers - e.g., responding to Slack messages / responding to emails / responding to support tickets
    • Advanced ability to use data and systems (e.g., CRM, log analysis tools) to monitor customer health, identify complex trends, and strategically inform customer success and retention initiatives.
    • Extensive experience crafting customer-facing artifacts and decks
    • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively engage and influence stakeholders at all levels of an organization, including C-suite executives.

We are Local Infusion.

Local Infusion is the fastest growing infusion provider in the United States, with a mission to transform the specialty infusion industry, because patients deserve better. By providing both exceptional, patient-centered care and the proprietary, AI-driven technology powering it, Local Infusion accelerates access, simplifies workflows, and improves outcomes for everyone in the infusion journey — from patients and clinicians to health plans, health systems, employers, and pharma.

Clinicians can spend less time on paperwork and more time with patients, bringing comfort, connection, and community back to healthcare. With Local Infusion, every patient and every care team is fully supported, every step of the way.

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Local Infusion will come exclusively from an @ email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them.

The Role

Local Infusion is building a next-generation operating system for infusion care — powered by automation, AI, and real-time insights. We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to own the intelligence layer of our platform. You’ll work across structured and unstructured data to drive automation, predict bottlenecks, and help patients start treatment faster.

Key Accountabilities:

  • Model Development: Build and deploy ML models to identify missing data, predict treatment delays, triage high-risk referrals, and score payer/patient friction

  • AI Integration: Architect and maintain LLM-powered workflows

  • Data Infrastructure: Build and maintain data pipelines to collect, clean, label, and store data across systems

  • Model Monitoring: Define success metrics, monitor model performance over time, and iterate quickly to improve accuracy and reliability. Set up training data, data labeling workflows or feedback loops for model improvement.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with product, engineering, and operations to identify high-leverage automation opportunities and embed models into workflows.

Key Requirements:

  • 6+ years in ML engineering, data science, or applied AI roles (bonus for healthcare experience).

  • Proficient in Python (Pandas, Scikit-learn, LangChain, PyTorch or TensorFlow) and SQL.

  • Strong experience building and deploying models in production environments.

  • Familiar with LLM integration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and vector search (e.g., Pinecone, FAISS).

  • Skilled in working with unstructured data: OCR, NLP, form/document understanding.

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred), Git, and basic DevOps practices.

  • Comfortable partnering with product and operations teams to solve real-world business problems.

  • Working with healthcare data (EMR/EHR, insurance claims, HL7/FHIR).

  • Building patient or payer-facing AI solutions in regulated environments (HIPAA).

The Local Infusion Way

Local Infusion is a respectful, upbeat, and remote-first team united by our mission of shaping the way specialty infusion care is delivered. We are highly ambitious but understand that in order to do a great job, we have to take care of ourselves; we expect that you will have time and energy devoted to your families, friends and hobbies.

As part of our team, full-time employees get:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance through our employer plan

  • Short and long-term disability coverage

  • 401(k) — as an early-stage startup, and we match!

  • 15 Days PTO — and we want you to take it!

  • Competitive paid parental leave and flexible return to work policy.

  • We invest in your career. Our company is growing quickly, and we'll give you the opportunity to do the same. You'll have access to a number of professional development opportunities so that you can keep up with the company's evolving needs and grow your career along the way.

We don’t discriminate—Local Infusion is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Employer. We fundamentally believe that a more diverse and inclusive team leads to a stronger company more able to achieve our vision.

What We're Researching

We are running a paid study on how public-facing experts gather information and stay informed on emerging issues. This research helps us understand the shifting landscape of knowledge distribution and trusted sourcing. Your insights will inform how we evaluate professional information-gathering habits across various fields.

How It Works

You will complete a short remote survey detailing your professional experience and information workflows. The survey asks you to walk through the sources you trust, how you verify facts, and the ways you share knowledge with your audience. You will react to different scenarios regarding emerging issues and explain your typical engagement strategies. The entire process is asynchronous and designed to be completed quickly on your own schedule.

Who This Is For

We are looking for influential professionals who actively shape public understanding or community discourse. We welcome educators, media professionals, nonprofit leaders, cultural institution directors, researchers, and community organizers. Ideal candidates regularly consume, synthesize, and distribute information to broader audiences in their daily work.

What You'll Do

  • Complete an asynchronous remote survey about your professional workflows

  • Detail how you access, verify, and engage with emerging issues

  • Describe the information sources you rely on most heavily in your field

  • Explain how you share synthesized knowledge with your community or audience

Who Should Apply

  • Current role in education, media, nonprofit, research, or community leadership

raw.description:
We are looking for a Senior Lead - Shared Services to join our Human Resources group; as we scale up and drive digital and financial inclusion across our markets.

Job Purpose

The Senior Lead – HR Shared Services is responsible for overseeing the delivery of efficient, accurate, and compliant HR operational services across the employee lifecycle. The role supports global and market-level HR operations, including employee records management, contracts administration, payroll input coordination, offboarding, and employee relations case administration.

The position drives operational excellence through strong service governance, stakeholder management, risk controls, and continuous process improvement while ensuring consistent delivery against agreed service standards and SLAs.

Key Responsibilities

1. Service Delivery Leadership & Governance

  • Oversee day-to-day HR Shared Services operations, ensuring timely and accurate execution of activities across the employee lifecycle.

  • Coordinate workload allocation, prioritisation, and operational follow-through across the function.

  • Establish and maintain operational routines, service standards, and process handoffs.

  • Track and report service KPIs including SLA adherence, turnaround times, quality metrics, backlog management, and error rates.

  • Manage escalations, resolve operational bottlenecks, and ensure timely communication and case closure.

2. Stakeholder Management & Cross-functional Coordination

  • Partner with People Partners, Talent Acquisition, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and HRIS teams to deliver seamless HR operational support.

  • Align stakeholders on timelines, approvals, documentation standards, and service expectations.

  • Translate policy or business changes into operational processes, templates, communications, and training materials.

  • Provide operational updates, risk reporting, and improvement recommendations to People leadership where required.

3. Records & Data Governance

  • Ensure employee records and documentation are complete, accurate, and compliant with internal and regulatory requirements.

  • Conduct regular audits to identify and resolve data inconsistencies or compliance gaps.

  • Maintain confidentiality and strong controls around employee data handling and storage.

  • Drive HR data quality initiatives and implement preventive controls to minimise recurring errors.

4. Contracts & Employment Lifecycle Administration

  • Oversee employment contract issuance, renewals, amendments, and extensions within established timelines.

  • Ensure all employee documentation is accurately maintained within HR systems and document repositories.

  • Manage probation administration processes including confirmations, extensions, and related approvals.

  • Support performance management cycle administration, including documentation, letters, approvals tracking, and records management.

  • Ensure compliance with approval workflows, documentation standards, and record retention requirements.

5. Payroll Input Coordination

  • Coordinate monthly payroll input readiness by managing timelines, approvals, and submission requirements.

  • Oversee preparation and validation of payroll-related inputs, including commissions, bonuses, and employee lifecycle changes.

  • Investigate payroll discrepancies and coordinate corrective actions with Payroll and Finance stakeholders.

  • Maintain audit-ready payroll documentation and supporting controls.

6. Offboarding Operations

  • Coordinate smooth employee offboarding processes, including exit documentation, systems updates, benefits cessation, and stakeholder handoffs.

  • Ensure offboarding activities are completed accurately and within required timelines.

  • Manage escalations and exceptions to minimise operational risk and maintain a positive employee experience.

7. Employee Relations Case Administration

  • Oversee administration of disciplinary and grievance cases, including documentation, scheduling, minutes, milestone tracking, and outcome communication.

  • Maintain secure and confidential employee relations records in line with company policies and compliance requirements.

  • Support maintenance of ER templates, SOPs, and operational guidance documentation.

  • Coordinate timely follow-up and closure of employee relations cases.

8. Continuous Improvement & Operational Controls

  • Identify operational inefficiencies and implement practical process improvements, templates, and standardisation initiatives.

  • Support process mapping, SOP documentation, and operational training activities.

  • Strengthen operational controls relating to approvals, documentation, segregation of duties, and audit readiness.

  • Drive adoption of process enhancements and ensure operational consistency across the function.

9. Data Analytics, Reporting & AI Enablement

  • Analyse operational service data to identify trends, bottlenecks, recurring issues, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Develop and maintain dashboards covering SLA performance, service quality, payroll exceptions, and case management metrics.

  • Partner with HRIS and People Systems teams to support automation and AI-enabled HR operations initiatives.

  • Ensure AI-enabled processes comply with data privacy, governance, and documentation standards.

  • Use operational insights to support decision-making and improve employee experience outcomes.

Reporting Structure

Reports To: Head of HR Shared Services

Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, or a related field.

Professional Certification

  • Certified HR Practitioner in Ghana, preferably CIHRM

Experience

  • 4–5 years’ experience in HR Shared Services, HR Operations, or employee lifecycle administration roles.

  • Hands-on experience across HR records management, contracts administration, payroll coordination, offboarding, and employee relations support.

  • Experience working within fast-paced or multi-country operational environments is an advantage.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong understanding of HR operations, compliance requirements, and employee lifecycle processes.

  • Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional coordination skills.

  • Close attention to detail with strong risk awareness and control discipline.

  • Strong analytical and reporting capabilities with experience using operational metrics to drive improvements.

  • Experience supporting automation, process improvement, or AI-enabled HR operational initiatives.

  • Strong communication, escalation management, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work within tight deadlines.

  • Experience using HRIS systems such as HiBob or equivalent platforms is preferred.

  • Familiarity with ticketing or case management systems such as Freshservice is an advantage.

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at .

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

Important Notice

M-KOPA is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to assembling a diverse, broadly trained staff. Women, minorities, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

M-KOPA explicitly prohibits the use of Forced or Child Labour and respects the rights of its employees to agree to terms and conditions of employment voluntarily, without coercion, and freely terminate their employment on appropriate notice. M-KOPA shall ensure that its Employees are of legal working age and shall comply with local laws for youth employment or student work, such as internships or apprenticeships.

M-KOPA does not collect/charge any money as a pre-employment or post-employment requirement. This means that we never ask for ‘recruitment fees’, ‘processing fees’, ‘interview fees’, or any other kind of money in exchange for offer letters or interviews at any time during the hiring process.

Applications for this position will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisting and interviews will take place at any stage during the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a suitable candidate is selected before the advertised closing date.

If your application is successful M-KOPA undertakes pre-employment background checks as part of its recruitment process, these include; criminal records, identification verification, academic qualifications, employment dates and employer references.

raw.description:
About the Role

This role sits at the intersection of robotics and data infrastructure at a well-funded, early-stage robotics company. You'll be responsible for building reliable pipelines and storage systems that make large volumes of robot telemetry and sensor data usable for engineering and ML teams. Your work will directly enable faster iteration and safer robotic systems — from raw sensor ingestion all the way through to training-ready datasets and real-time analytics.

You'll join a cross-functional team of robotics engineers, software engineers, and data scientists in a fast-paced, on-site environment in Los Angeles, CA. This is a high-impact, hands-on role with broad scope at a company building at the frontier of physical AI and robotics.

Please note: Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build scalable data pipelines to ingest and process robot telemetry and sensor data (camera, LiDAR, IMU, and more).

  • Implement storage solutions and schemas that support analytics, model training, and data replay.

  • Ensure data quality, validation, and lineage across ingestion and transformation stages.

  • Optimize latency and throughput for both real-time and batch processing use cases.

  • Instrument observability, monitoring, and alerting for data flows and infrastructure.

  • Collaborate closely with robotics engineers and data scientists to translate platform needs into production-grade implementations.

  • Productionize ETL/ELT workflows with CI/CD and automated testing.

  • Troubleshoot and resolve production incidents affecting data availability or correctness.

What We're Looking For

Required:

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience building data infrastructure or engineering pipelines specifically for robotics sensor data — this is a dealbreaker requirement.

  • Proven experience designing, building, and maintaining data ingestion, processing, and storage pipelines for sensor data (e.g., camera, LiDAR, IMU).

  • Strong fundamentals in distributed systems, databases, and data pipeline design.

  • Proficiency in Python and/or C++ for building data tooling and pipelines.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud data platforms and distributed processing tools — e.g., AWS or GCP, Kafka or Pub/Sub, Spark or Flink, Airflow.

  • Experience with containerization and deployment of data pipelines using Docker and Kubernetes, plus basic CI/CD.

  • Experience with time-series databases and telemetry data management in a robotics context.

  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset for working across engineering and ML teams.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with ROS / ROS2 robotics middleware.

  • Familiarity with ML workflow tooling such as MLFlow or Kubeflow for end-to-end robotics data pipelines.

  • Experience with robotics simulation tools (e.g., Gazebo) and synthetic data generation.

  • Prior experience in an early-stage or high-growth startup environment.

Location

This is a full-time, on-site role based in Los Angeles, CA. Candidates based in or willing to relocate to the Los Angeles area are strongly preferred. The company also has a presence in New York City, NY and San Francisco, CA.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation will be competitive and commensurate with experience, including equity participation appropriate for an early-stage company. Specific details will be shared during the interview process.

raw.description:
About Clarity Pediatrics
Clarity Pediatrics is building a new model for pediatric chronic care — one that brings affordable, science-backed care to the 1 in 3 kids with chronic conditions. We deliver virtual, evidence-based care that’s accessible, collaborative, and designed to support families and providers alike. We’ve started with ADHD and anxiety, and we’re working to expand into other chronic conditions like asthma, allergies, and obesity. Backed by $10M from leading healthcare investors, we’re led by experienced clinicians and healthcare leaders with deep domain expertise and a shared commitment to clinical excellence.

Our Culture

We’re building a team of clinicians who are collaborative, curious, and committed to delivering exceptional care. Here’s what you can expect:

  • Co-founded by a pediatric provider, with exceptional clinical leaders including licensed mental health providers in key roles shaping every major decision

  • Clinical model built to partner closely with referring providers

  • Multidisciplinary collaboration and robust case consultation opportunities

  • A diverse, inclusive, and mission-driven community where your voice matters

  • Access to expert clinical guidance from ADHD and anxiety specialists and researchers

  • Ongoing opportunities for professional growth and training

What We Offer

We’re committed to taking care of the healthcare providers who care for our patients. Our benefits include:

  • Fully remote and flexible schedule

  • Salary $85,000-$110,000/year (full-time)

  • Available bonus opportunities

  • Medical, dental, vision, and ancillary benefits

  • 401(k)

  • Flexible PTO

  • CME/CEU support and reimbursement

  • Remote-friendly work culture

  • A dedicated care coordination team to support with administrative tasks (e.g., cancellations, rescheduling, documentation requests, billing)

  • And more—we’re growing and evolving, so tell us what matters most to you!

About the Role

Clarity Pediatrics is seeking full time, licensed Child and Family Therapists to join our remote, multidisciplinary team. You’ll provide clinical services including ADHD and anxiety assessments and leading parenting groups such as Parent Training in Behavior Management (BPT) and Supportive Parenting for Anxious Childhood Emotion (SPACE).

We’re committed to setting clinicians up for success with peer consultation groups, guidance from ADHD and anxiety experts, and stipends for professional development. You’ll also have the opportunity to shape our care model and improve workflows that support high-quality, sustainable care. We value diverse clinical backgrounds and encourage you to grow your expertise, lead initiatives, and focus on what you do best.

With our full time (40 hr/week) role, enjoy flexible scheduling within our operating hours (weekdays 8 am – 8 pm and Saturdays), in the time zone where you provide care.

What You’ll Own

  • Conduct comprehensive ADHD and anxiety assessments and intake evaluations for new patients and families

  • Provide personalized treatment recommendations, including referrals to community providers when appropriate

  • Lead group therapy sessions for caregivers of children with ADHD, anxiety, and co-occurring conditions such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)

  • Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to deliver high-quality, integrated care

  • Opportunities exist to contribute to program development, evaluation, and research initiatives—based on your interests and organizational needs

About You

  • You’re a licensed mental health professional (LPCC, LMFT, or LCSW) with a master’s degree in a relevant field—and you're passionate about providing excellent care to kids and families.

  • You’re currently licensed in California and open to getting licensed in other states (we’ll support you with that!)

  • You have experience working in integrated care settings and enjoy using evidence-based approaches, especially for pediatric ADHD and anxiety.

  • You’re tech-savvy, a quick learner, and excited about shaping the future of behavioral health through innovative, virtual care.

  • You’re energized by collaboration and interested in building better systems—whether through care model design, new tools, or team initiatives.

  • This role is remote, so you’re able to work from a private, secure location with strong internet—and you’re open to working at least 2 hours per week during peak times (M-F 6:00-8pm PT, and/or Saturday 8am-2pm)

  • Spanish proficiency

Nice to Have

  • Licensed in additional states
